ruling: RETIRE PERMANENTLY — do not replace with a local cron.
question_answered: code-janitor system-issue cj-20260812T043111Z asked PO to choose between (a) replace docs/agent-memory/health/team-tool-recheck-*.md's writer with a local cron per the no-RemoteTrigger migration rule, or (b) retire the team-tool-recheck permanently and let memory-prune-sweep.sh's 30d rule drain the directory to empty. PO selects (b).
rationale: The writer was cloud RemoteTrigger trig_019Q8D5xttjZn6iytx2Ld9dW, killed by the 2026-06-22 standing no-RemoteTrigger directive. It has been silent ~7 weeks with zero observed consequence.

Its function — verifying that each agent's granted tool surface matches what its flow actually demands — is now covered by live, board-tracked work that did not exist when the recheck was written: FIX-ORPHAN-FR7-VERIFY-TOOL-REGISTRY (DONE_VERIFIED 2026-08-11) and FIX-AGENT-BASH-GRANT-COVERAGE-GATE-FLOW-DEMANDS-VS-FRONTMATTER (backlog, P1, next=agent-father). Re-arming the recheck would create a second, weaker authority over the same question.

Adding a 5th standalone cron to re-derive something two ratified mechanisms already own is net negative: more cron surface to keep armed across session restarts (/cron-standalone-team), more fire-gap signals when it drifts, no new information.
The 30d prune rule already drains the directory correctly. No migration work is required — retirement is the null action plus this ruling.
action_for_code_janitor: Stop raising this decision. Let memory-prune-sweep.sh's existing 30d rule drain docs/agent-memory/health/team-tool-recheck-*.md to empty. No local cron is to be created.

known_defect_observed_while_ruling.summary: This marker's own idempotency mechanism does not survive signal drain.
known_defect_observed_while_ruling.detail: scripts/agents-flow/memory-prune-sweep.sh:109 guards on `find "$SIGNALS_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'janitor-health-recheck-writer-retired-*.json'`. The routine signal drain moves processed signals into docs/signals/processed/, which -maxdepth 1 cannot see. A prior marker already exists at docs/signals/processed/janitor-health-recheck-writer-retired-2026-08-05.json, which is exactly why this decision was re-raised on 2026-08-12 despite having been marked once already. This file will be drained the same way and the question will be asked again.
known_defect_observed_while_ruling.durable_fix: Either drop -maxdepth 1 so the guard also matches docs/signals/processed/, or move the retired-marker state out of the signal bus entirely (it is durable configuration, not a transient signal — the signal bus is the wrong store for it).
known_defect_observed_while_ruling.owner_note: Recorded here rather than minted as a board row: it is a one-predicate change in a script whose next toucher reads this file by construction. If it recurs a third time, mint it.
